assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin biology, proglucagon processing, active GLP-1(7-36) amide) led directly to therapies that transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Original, clear, and of very large clinical reach.
assessment.attribution: Holst (incretin physiology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and translation) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) form a plausible trio. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen's drug-development role (liraglutide, semaglutide) is real but industrial; the list supplied does not include Joel Habener, whose role I recall but cannot verify against the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of clinical trials and real-world use, independent confirmation across many drugs and indications. Timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between Mojsov and the Habener group is contested; as I recall it, and without independent verification.
The drug-development contribution (Knudsen) may be seen as separate from the discovery science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA is sensed and converted into type I interferon and inflammatory responses. It is central to antiviral defence, cancer immunity and autoinflammatory and autoimmune disease (interferonopathies, lupus), where I see its relevance directly.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP; Barber identified STING. Ishikawa co-identified STING and Sun and Wu worked with Chen, so the allocation among five credited names is hard; two core names best reflect the two decisive steps.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, structural and genetic validation, and wide follow-up. Therapeutic translation (STING agonists and antagonists) is still immature, but the discovery itself is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for STING discovery is split between Barber and Ishikawa, and Sun and Wu are also credited on cGAS; limited to three laureates.
Clinical benefit has not yet been demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and now myeloma, and are being tested in autoimmune disease. A new therapeutic modality with clear impact.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical translation), Sadelain (CD28 co-stimulation and CAR design) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy, early gene-modified TIL) cover distinct stages. Others who contributed (Eshhar, Kuwana, Brenner) are not in the supplied list.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and years of follow-up; durability and toxicity are well characterised. Solid-tumour efficacy remains limited.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be framed as cell therapy or CAR design affects the laureate choice.
Early CAR concept credit (Eshhar and others) is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The division of lymphocytes into thymus-derived T and bursa/bone-marrow-derived B cells is foundational to adaptive immunity and underpins vaccines, immunodeficiency diagnosis, and immunotherapy. A classic, clear, original discovery.
assessment.attribution: Miller defined the thymus function in cell-mediated immunity; Cooper (with Good and Peterson) showed the bursa and B-cell lineage. A clean two-person configuration is supported by the supplied credit; Robert Good is deceased.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and universally confirmed; recognition is arguably overdue, with advancing age of the laureates a pressure.
uncertainties: Whether Cooper's contribution is judged as independent of Good and Peterson's earlier work, which cannot be recognised posthumously.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identifying TNF as the dominant driver of synovial inflammation and showing in patients that blocking it works changed rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn's disease, psoriasis and other conditions. A rare mechanism-to-clinic proof-of-concept in chronic inflammation.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly developed the concept and ran the initial clinical trials; the pairing is well established. Other contributors to TNF biology and antibody engineering exist outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with decades of use and biosimilars; the field's value is beyond doubt. I disclose that I work in rheumatology, but I judge this on the shared criteria.
uncertainties: Prior Lasker recognition suggests the case is well-known but this does not settle Nobel priority against other immunology candidates.
Credit for the TNF antibody engineering may be viewed as separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib's targeting of BCR-ABL turned chronic myeloid leukemia from fatal to manageable and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound development), Druker (preclinical and clinical proof) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) cover the key stages. Earlier discoveries of BCR-ABL (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore) are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with long-term survival data and independent replication; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Foundational BCR-ABL oncogene discoveries are separate from the therapeutic story and may complicate the framing.
Sawyers' role is mainly in resistance and next-generation drugs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-organising organoids grown from single Lgr5-positive adult stem cells created a durable platform for studying epithelium, modelling disease, and testing drugs in patient-derived tissue.
assessment.attribution: Clevers established the Lgr5 stem cell and the organoid culture; Sato made the key early demonstration of intestinal organoids. The two-person configuration fits the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted, with independent confirmation, but clinical impact is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical translation and regenerative applications remain limited.
Related organoid work by others (for example Sasai) falls outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin and its adaptation as a genetically targeted tool allow causal manipulation of defined neural circuits and have changed experimental neuroscience and physiology.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann characterised channelrhodopsin; Deisseroth (with Boyden) developed neuronal application. Six credited names exceed the maximum of three, with Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck all strongly arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a research tool with massive uptake; clinical use (retinal gene therapy) is only beginning.
uncertainties: The three-laureate limit makes allocation very contested.
It is a tool rather than a disease mechanism, which some members may weigh differently.
